summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted for acute shortness of breath and severe hypertension, with initial presentation of pulmonary edema. She had recently undergone dialysis but developed fluid overload, leading to flash pulmonary edema. She was stabilized with blood pressure management and a session of hemodialysis, after which her respiratory symptoms resolved. Her INR was found to be supratherapeutic at 4.1, prompting a two-day hold on warfarin, with plans to restart post-discharge. She remained hemodynamically stable, with no evidence of infection or acute coronary syndrome. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to restart anticoagulation, monitor INR, adhere to fluid and sodium restrictions, and follow up with her specialists.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
